tagline: A complete environment for every pull request, destroyed the moment the branch merges.
overview: Reviewing a change from a screenshot or a shared staging box hides the bugs that only appear when the whole stack is running. We give each pull request its own namespace or stack: application, database, queues, seeded test data and a URL the reviewer opens in a browser. Nothing is shared with staging, so two branches cannot interfere with each other.

The engineering is mostly in the lifecycle. Environments are created by the pipeline, seeded from anonymised production-shaped data, labelled with an expiry, and reclaimed automatically so the cloud bill stays flat. We also plan the awkward cases: migrations that must run against the new schema, third-party callbacks that need a stable hostname, and services too expensive to duplicate on every branch.
problems: Everyone tests on the same staging box and overwrites each other
Test data is stale, hand-built and looks nothing like production
Branches stay open for weeks, so environment costs pile up
Reviewers approve changes they have never actually run

includes.title: Per-pull-request stacks
includes.text: A namespace or stack created on open and reviewed on a unique URL, with the application, database and dependencies deployed together and no crossover with staging.

includes.title: Seed data pipeline
includes.text: Anonymised subsets of realistic data loaded into each environment, refreshed on a schedule, so tests exercise the volumes and edge cases production actually contains.

includes.title: Automatic teardown
includes.text: Environments expire when the branch merges or after a fixed idle period, with a warning first, so nothing is left running because someone forgot.

includes.title: Isolation by default
includes.text: Separate credentials, separate databases and network rules that prevent a preview environment from reaching production data or a colleague's stack.

includes.title: Stable routing
includes.text: Predictable hostnames and wildcard DNS so webhooks, OAuth callbacks and third-party integrations point somewhere consistent instead of a new address on every push.

includes.title: Cost controls
includes.text: Resource quotas, small instance types and scheduled shutdown for idle environments, with the running cost of previews reported alongside the rest of your cloud spend.

deliverables: Environment template for one service or full stack
Seed and anonymisation scripts for test data
Pipeline jobs for create, update and teardown
Expiry and idle-shutdown policy with alerting
Preview URL convention and access control rules

process.title: Map the review needs
process.text: We find out which changes actually need a running stack and which dependencies have to be real, rather than assuming every service can be duplicated cheaply.

process.title: Build the environment template
process.text: Helm charts, Terraform or manifests that stand up the stack from scratch in minutes, parameterised per branch and tested on a throwaway environment.

process.title: Solve data and routing
process.text: Seed jobs load a realistic dataset, wildcard DNS gives each environment a stable hostname, and secrets are scoped so previews cannot touch production.

process.title: Automate the lifecycle
process.text: Creation on pull request, updates on each push, teardown on merge and a nightly sweep for anything that outlived its branch.

faqs.q: Can every service get a preview environment?
faqs.a: Not realistically. Stateful services, expensive data warehouses and anything with a licensed dependency often cannot be duplicated per branch. We identify those first and provide a shared alternative, so the environments you do get are trustworthy.

faqs.q: How do you keep test data realistic without copying production?
faqs.a: We take a production-shaped subset, replace direct identifiers with generated values, and keep the statistical distribution intact. Referential integrity is preserved so joins still work, and the transformation runs on a schedule rather than by hand.

faqs.q: Will this make our cloud bill go up?
faqs.a: Per-preview cost is real, and pretending otherwise is dishonest. We offset it with small instance sizes, idle shutdown and expiry rules, and the savings from people no longer keeping a shared staging stack running around the clock.

faqs.q: Do reviewers need to know Kubernetes to use them?
faqs.a: No. The reviewer gets a URL and a login. Everything below that is the platform's problem, and we write the pipeline so engineers can change the environment definition without understanding the whole cluster.

seo.title: Ephemeral & Preview Environments for Every Pull Request
seo.description: Isolated per-branch environments with seeded test data, stable URLs and automatic teardown, so reviewers test the real stack before they approve a change.
